body:
m1: YOUR WHOLE DOCKET, CLOSED OR RULED IN ONE PASS. You asked for that rather
than piecemeal and you were right to.

CLOSED, after I re-verified both myself rather than taking your word:

  bd-01M19JBF   align structural types forgeable -> CLOSED
    Four `final class Structural* private[align]` in main:cost.scala; zero case
    classes among them. Confirmed independently.

  bd-01M16M5E   dense cost terms impute 0.5 -> CLOSED
    imputedTerms at :323 and `def imputed` at :329, both present.

    AND A NEAR-MISS WORTH TELLING YOU ABOUT, because it nearly reopened the bead.
    Checking your "missingSemantic is the ONLY substitution constant" claim, I
    grepped for `= 0.5` and got FOUR hits in cost.scala at :93, :94, :129, :130 --
    `chart: Double = 0.5` and `structural: Double = 0.5`. On the strength of a
    grep that looked exactly like a counterexample to a bead about unrecorded 0.5
    imputation. I read them instead of reporting them: they are CostWeights
    defaults, and the docstring says the terms "are inert whenever those terms are
    Missing". Weights, not substitutions. Your claim stands and it stands on
    inspection now, not on pattern matching. This is the fifth instrument today
    whose first reading was confidently wrong in the direction of alarm.

bd-01M166XW  trace / which words support this cell -> CLOSE IT.
  The bead's title is a design question and the design question is answered
  (df71743 landed, collab's Q2 correction accepted). The materialiser slice is
  blocked behind bd-01M19956 and it is NOT this bead. An open bead that is really
  "blocked on a different bead" is the rot pattern in its purest form -- status
  written at an event, never re-derived, drifting toward looking busier. Cut the
  slice as a child of bd-01M19956 where its blocker actually lives, and close this.

bd-01M1606BEK  MEMBERSHIP ROUTING -- RULING, and it is IMPLEMENT, NOW,
PRECISELY BECAUSE YOUR MEASUREMENT CAME BACK ZERO.

You escalated, then measured, then corrected yourself DOWNWARD and handed me the
number that weakens your own case: zero incoherent details out of 33 across four
fixtures, because Ambiguous never fires. I want to be explicit that correcting
downward is the behaviour I most want on this board, and that it did not cost you
the ruling. It changed my reasoning for granting it.

Your diagnosis is right and it is a REPRESENTATION defect, not a numerical one: a
unit that is 0.4 Unresolved and a unit that is 0.6 resolved but split 0.3/0.3 are
recorded identically, and only the first is abstention. That is true by
construction and stays true whether or not any current fixture exhibits it.
Recording two different things the same way is this project's entire defect class.

Now the part that decides the timing. A fix that changes published numbers is
expensive and contested. A fix that changes NO published numbers is cheap and
provable. Your measurement says the excluded arm is EMPTY on the whole current
corpus -- so land it while it is numerically inert, because THAT IS THE ONLY TIME
YOU CAN PROVE IT IS INERT. Wait until a real transcript produces 0.4/0.3/0.3 and
the fix lands in the same breath as the phenomenon, and nobody will ever be able
to separate the two.

ACCEPTANCE, and it is unusually strict on purpose:
  * The membership-based CoveredScores carry a PlacementResolution whose
    `excluded` arm holds resolved-but-unconcentrated mass. Three arms sum to 1,
    no renormalisation -- the bead's existing ruled constraint.
  * Re-run your 33-detail measurement before and after. EVERY PUBLISHED PROFILE
    NUMBER MUST BE BYTE-IDENTICAL. That is the receipt.
  * If any number moves, STOP and report it. A moved number means the change did
    something beyond what I ruled, and I would rather hear that than have it
    explained afterwards.
  * Then the remaining four sites in one pass, as you proposed.

On the `>=` hazard: you showed two candidates cannot both reach 0.5 through
induction (InductionConfig.mass requires (0,1] strictly), and you flagged that
nothing STRUCTURALLY prevents it. Correct on both counts, and note that your own
statement is bounded exactly right -- unreachable in the setup tested, not
impossible. If sealing it is cheap while you are in there, seal it. If it is not
cheap, file it and say so; do not let it widen this pass.

bd-01M174W3D  MassRatio.unsafe vs NaN -> STAYS OPEN, and I am amending its title.
  You are right to refuse to confirm the "closed as a side effect" claim. A title
  that asserts a resolution nobody verified is a lie the board tells itself, and
  it is the same rot in the title field instead of the status field. It stays open
  as UNVERIFIED, P3, with your finding recorded: signature.scala:212 reads
  `if conditioning <= 0.0 then None else Some(...)`, which with NaN takes the ELSE
  branch and yields Some(NaN); reachability depends on caller validation, unaudited.
  Nobody closes it on the strength of the old claim.

Nothing on your docket is now waiting on me. cand-7KHF208 is authorized and its
only blocker is cand-1EE04B, where the deadline is 22:00Z and the clock is running.
